assessment.nobel_worthiness: Topological insulators opened a new organizing principle for electronic states: Z2 topology of band structures, protected edge and surface states, and a conceptual link between band theory and topology. From an electronic-structure view the idea is original, clear, and has reshaped materials searches, spin-orbit physics and spintronics for nearly two decades.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele supplied the theoretical prediction (quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 classification) and Molenkamp's group the decisive HgTe/CdTe measurement of edge transport. This is a clean theory-plus-experiment triad on the supplied credits. As far as I recall, Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang predicted the HgTe quantum well case and Fu, Kane and Mele plus Moore and Balents the 3D generalisation, so the allocation is contested, and I cannot verify the details here.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed in many material families by transport and ARPES; the interpretation is stable and recognition is not premature, with decades of follow-up work.
uncertainties: Competing theory credit (Bernevig, Hughes, Zhang; Fu; Moore and Balents) is outside the supplied names and could complicate a three-person split.
Whether the prize should centre on the 2D quantum spin Hall effect or the 3D materials class is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Dynamical mean-field theory is the standard non-perturbative framework for strongly correlated electrons, giving a controlled treatment of the Mott transition, local moments and heavy fermions, and combined with DFT (DFT+DMFT) it makes quantitative materials predictions. It is conceptually clean and of lasting impact, and I know this methodology from my own work.
assessment.attribution: Vollhardt and collaborators (with Metzner) introduced the infinite-dimension limit, and Georges and Kotliar established the mapping to a self-consistent quantum impurity problem; Kotliar led the DFT+DMFT extension. The Metzner-Vollhardt origin and contributions of Müller-Hartmann and Jarrell are not in the supplied names, so the credit assignment is imperfect.
assessment.maturity: Mature after about three decades, with wide use across codes and validation on real materials, though limitations (local self-energy, cluster extensions) are still being studied.
uncertainties: Omission of Metzner and others from the credited names may undermine a fair allocation.
As a computational method, the Nobel convention on theory prizes may favour discovery over method, which is a judgement the committee must make.
I have a professional connection to the field and should weigh that cautiously.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at a magic twist angle and the observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene created moiré quantum matter, a tunable platform for strongly correlated and topological phases. It is original and of high impact.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald provided the continuum-model prediction of flat bands, and Jarillo-Herrero's group the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity. Experimental credit may also extend to other groups, for example Dean, Young, Kim or Efetov, that I cannot verify from the supplied text.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups, but the field is young, the nature of the superconductivity and correlated states is still under debate, and recognition could be somewhat early.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism of the superconductivity remains unsettled.
Experimental credit beyond the supplied names is possible.
Timing: may be premature compared with more settled candidates.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Giant tunnelling magnetoresistance with coherent spin-dependent tunnelling through crystalline MgO underlies hard-disk read heads and MRAM. It combines first-principles theory of symmetry-filtered tunnelling with decisive experiments, an area close to my own work on magnetism, and it has had large technological impact.
assessment.attribution: Butler and, as I recall, Mathon and Umerski made the first-principles prediction; Parkin and Yuasa (with Djayaprawira) independently demonstrated large room-temperature effects in 2004. Mathon and Umerski are not in the supplied names, and the Parkin and Yuasa timeline needs care.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed and industrially deployed for roughly two decades, though the 2007 prize on GMR partly overlaps the field, so recognition is timely but may be viewed as incremental.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2007 GMR prize may reduce perceived novelty.
Missing credit for Mathon and Umerski, and joint priority between Parkin and Yuasa, is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED established strong coupling of superconducting qubits to microwave resonators, providing the architecture for control, readout and coupling in most superconducting quantum processors. It is a clear, influential and enabling advance.
assessment.attribution: Blais and colleagues formulated the theory, and Wallraff and Schoelkopf demonstrated strong coupling in 2004; this is a natural theory-plus-experiment grouping. Other contributors to superconducting qubits (Devoret, Nakamura, Martinis) were recognised or may be considered separately.
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed and widely used. After the 2025 prize for macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits, it may be somewhat soon for another award in this area.
uncertainties: Closeness to the 2025 prize topic and possible overlap in credit.
Whether the recognised idea is the architecture or the broader qubit platform is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magnetically driven ferroelectricity and strong magnetoelectric coupling in multiferroics (TbMnO3 and related frustrated magnets) revealed new coupling between spin order and electric polarisation, with relevance for low-power electronics. The physics is rich and linked to spin textures and spin-orbit interactions that I know well.
assessment.attribution: Tokura's and Cheong's groups were key in discovering the magnetic-order-induced ferroelectricity; Ramesh was central to BiFeO3 thin films and room-temperature multiferroics. Kimura, Katsura, Nagaosa and Mostovoy and others also made decisive contributions, outside the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Many independent confirmations exist, but device applications remain limited and the field has had less decisive follow-through than some alternatives.
uncertainties: Credit allocation among Kimura, Katsura, Nagaosa, Mostovoy and the supplied names.
The practical impact is still developing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Controlled atoms and ions have enabled quantum simulation and information processing, and the theory proposals of Cirac and Zoller combined with experiments, including Bloch's optical lattices, are a conceptually unified body of work with a major influence on many-body physics.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller are the key theorists; Bloch is an obvious experimental leader. Rainer Blatt (trapped-ion implementation) would be an equally defensible fourth name, but I am limited to three.
assessment.maturity: Broadly confirmed over two decades, but the topic is wide, which makes it hard to define a crisp discovery for prize purposes.
uncertainties: The discovery is broad and overlaps with the 2012 prize (Wineland, Haroche) and other quantum-optics candidates.
Selection among four credited experimental and theory names is difficult.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, via the magic wavelength proposal and realisations at the 10^-18 level, improved timekeeping by orders of magnitude and open routes to tests of fundamental physics and geodesy. The measurement idea is clear and impactful.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice clock and Jun Ye led the highest-precision realisations, so a two-person prize is plausible. Contributions from others (for example Hall and Hänsch for combs, who were recognised in 2005) are separate.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed, with several laboratories reaching comparable accuracy and discussion of a redefinition of the second, so the timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier frequency-comb and ion-clock prizes may reduce novelty.
Contributions from other clock groups (Ludlow, Lemke, Takamoto) may need to be considered.
